body: ## Spec — Filter the invoices table by status `wi_01M7YHSC5JSQYD8BGC6S7G68SW` · pipeline `product_work` · passes `bsf spec check` ### Plan Today `/invoices` always renders all five seeded invoices and there is no way to narrow the table. After this change, a row of five links sits above the table — **All, Draft, Sent, Paid, Void** — each navigating to `/invoices` with a `?status=` query parameter (All links to `/invoices` with no parameter), and the table renders only invoices with the selected status. The selected link is marked `aria-current="page"` and rendered at `fontWeight: 700` while the others are `400`, so it looks selected. A missing or unrecognised `?status=` value shows everything, which is the All state. The filter is read in the page only. `lib/invoices.ts` gains `INVOICE_STATUSES`, an `InvoiceStatus` type alias (which `Invoice.status` now uses, so the four statuses have one source of truth), `parseStatus()` to turn a raw query value into a status or `undefined`, and `invoicesWithStatus()` to filter — matching this repo's pattern of pure functions over `readonly` data in `lib/`. The export is deliberately untouched: `app/invoices/export/route.ts` and `components/ExportButton.tsx` are not in the files list, and the page keeps passing `count={exportableInvoices(listInvoices()).length}` computed from the full list, not the filtered one. The button still says "Export 3 invoices as CSV" and still downloads the same three sent/paid rows under every filter. The filter links stay inline in `app/invoices/page.tsx` rather than becoming `components/StatusFilter.tsx`: the feature map says a component moves to `components/` only on a second use or when it needs browser APIs, and this is one page with no browser APIs. **Not in scope**, and worth its own work item if wanted: making the export respect the filter, and persisting or combining filters. ### Files the build may touch | File | Why | | --- | --- | | `lib/invoices.ts` | `INVOICE_STATUSES`, `InvoiceStatus`, `parseStatus()`, `invoicesWithStatus()` | | `app/invoices/page.tsx` | async page reading `searchParams`, the filter nav, the table renders the filtered list | | `lib/invoices.test.ts` | extended — declared in `tests_changed` | | `app/invoices/page.test.tsx` | new | Feature folders: `lib/`, `app/invoices/`. ### Acceptance checks 1. Load `/invoices` with no query parameter: the table body shows all five seeded invoices (INV-1001 ... INV-1005), and five links labelled exactly All, Draft, Sent, Paid, Void appear above the table. 2. Click **Draft** (or load `/invoices?status=draft`): the table body shows exactly one row, INV-1004; the other four are absent from the page. 3. `/invoices?status=paid`: the table body shows exactly two rows, INV-1001 and INV-1003. 4. `/invoices?status=sent`: exactly one row, INV-1002. `/invoices?status=void`: exactly one row, INV-1005. 5. On `/invoices?status=paid` the served HTML renders the Paid anchor with `aria-current="page"` and `font-weight:700`, and the other four carry no `aria-current` and `font-weight:400`; a screenshot shows Paid visibly bolder. 6. `/invoices?status=bogus`: all five invoices are shown and **All** is the anchor carrying `aria-current="page"` — an unrecognised status falls back to All rather than emptying the table or erroring. 7. On `/invoices?status=draft` the export button still reads "Export 3 invoices as CSV" (not 1), and clicking it downloads a CSV of the header row plus INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003 — identical to the unfiltered download. 8. `npm run build` exits 0 and lists `/invoices` as `ƒ (Dynamic)` rather than `○ (Static)`, the expected consequence of reading `searchParams`; `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` all exit 0. ### What the research settled A prototype of this change was built, typechecked, linted, tested and served over HTTP here, then reverted — so the plan is not a guess: - **`searchParams` is a `Promise` in Next 15.** The generated page type is `searchParams: Promise>` (`node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-utils/typegen.js:590`, next 15.5.29). The page becomes `async`, and `parseStatus` must accept `string | string[] | undefined`. - **Reading `searchParams` flips `/invoices` from static to dynamic** in the build output. The build still succeeds. This is expected and must not be worked around with `export const dynamic` or by reading the query on the client — hence check 8. - **An async server-component page is testable** under the existing vitest + jsdom + Testing Library setup, by awaiting the component and rendering the element it returns; `next/link` renders a plain `` with no app-router context and does not throw. Six such tests passed. No new dependency. - **Coverage is satisfiable.** The repo has no page test today, so without one the page's new lines would be entirely uncovered and the 80% diff-coverage gate would fail. With the prototype tests, `app/invoices/page.tsx` and `lib/invoices.ts` both hit 100% lines. - **Served over HTTP**, `?status=draft` listed only INV-1004, `?status=paid` listed INV-1001 and INV-1003, `?status=bogus` listed all five, and the nav rendered `Void` with the other four at `font-weight:400`. Every acceptance check above is exercisable at this sandbox's `renders` tier. - **The export did not move**: under `?status=draft` the label stayed "Export 3 invoices as CSV" and `GET /invoices/export` still returned the header row plus INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003. No protected path is touched and nothing here contradicts a stated practice (`practices.md` is currently empty). > Generated by [Spec](https://github.com/bsf-fixtures/ts-webapp/actions/runs/44883339759) · claude · opus50 · \~113 AIC · ⌖ \~21 AIC · ⊞ 2.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Absf-fixtures%2Fts-webapp+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+bsf-fixtures%2Fts-webapp%2Ffactory-role-spec%22&type=issues)
